chapter_title: The Chapter of the Elements that wept
spiritual_reading:
# The Four Griefs of the External Truths

**¶2.** The external truths that proceed from the Lord's inmost celestial nature — the truths that clothe the Divine Human — passed through three states of deep anguish. After the third they came to rest. Yet there remains a fourth grief, for they will grieve at the final consummation. And only then shall their lamentation cease, and they shall never again pass through such anguish from that time onward.

**¶3.** The first grief arose when they perceived the oncoming falsity from evil — the hostile power about to erupt against them. They had full perception of everything that would befall them. They were aware of the nature of the evil that would rise and assail them, yet by the necessity of divine providence they advanced toward it and entered spiritual combat with it. They prevailed over it; they held it fast. They confined and restrained it within the very forms of their own exterior being, within the structures through which they operate. They overcame its spiritual death, its self-love, and its falsity.

**¶4.** [GAP-1] The second grief came when [GAP-2] their origin, the Lord's inmost celestial nature, ascended out of the deepest state of falsity and evil, and left the external truths behind — that is, the moment when He divested Himself of them [GAP-3] and left them in the lower degrees. Indeed, when they perceived how the Divine Celestial had risen out of that abyss and departed from them, and that they were left behind amid the opposition of evil, [GAP-4: …the external truths surrendered] their will to every suffering. They remained behind and grew infirm beneath the pressure of the immense burden of all the labors of regeneration, until the final state.

**¶5.** [GAP-5] The third grief came when the Divine Proceeding stripped away the three external truths of active operation and placed them beneath all other degrees. He gave them an influx — a sign — to lift their perception upward and ascend toward interior states from that lowest place, and to pass through every natural state of the mind until they should arrive at the celestial state of tranquility and peace — the state of rest prepared for them. Yet when they perceived that He had separated Himself from them, while they themselves remained behind and had not ascended, at that moment these three operative truths grieved deeply. After their lamentation, they turned their will toward all the interior celestial states that had been concealed from them, and they came into unanimous accord. For [GAP-6] they were to ascend and reach the interior heights, and pass beyond all natural states until the appointed time that was ordained for them all [GAP-7: …to be fulfilled] at the consummation of all spiritual ages.

**¶6.** The fourth grief shall come when the Grand Human Form — the collective image of all regenerated good and truth — is taken up at the last judgment, and the external truths will grieve [GAP-8] over the souls of those who are in falsity from profanation and blasphemy against the Divine; for they may offer [GAP-9: …no further means of restoration] because those souls' living connections to the Divine Human have been severed [GAP-10: …and given over to] falsity from evil. And those souls likewise — when the Grand Human ascends and they are left alone — they will grieve because they will remain behind in torment forever. For they will be cut off and separated from the completed Divine Human Form. And it is an immutable consequence that these souls who are destined for spiritual death receive the retribution corresponding to the deeds they have done. They pass into that falsity from evil and are bound permanently with it — just as they desired it and loved it and invested their ruling love in it. At the very moment when the completed Divine Human rises up, they will grieve. And then they will cry out in anguish because they will be severed from the communion of this great Divine Human Form. And they remain behind forever. This great anguish [GAP-11: …of final separation] is terrible; it unfolds before the souls and [GAP-12: …the spirits] who are destined for spiritual death in accordance with their deeds. And they [GAP-13] will grieve with that grief and will never be silent, because rest shall not come to them from that time onward.

**¶7.** Thus these external truths belong to these very constituent principles of the created order. This fourth state of grief is the most heart-rending for them. It is far worse than the three preceding states. For in this fourth grief, the external truths do not grieve for themselves. Rather, they grieve and are stricken in will on account of those souls who will be permanently severed from peace — because rest shall never come about for them, so as to release them from torment for eternity.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: The garments, the sons of the First Man, wept bitterly three times. Then they were silent. There is a fourth time of weeping, for they will weep at the end. And then their crying can stop, and they will never again weep from this time on.

Now, the first time of their weeping is when they had seen the darkness, the enemy being about to burst out against them. They understood everything that would happen to them. They were aware of the one that would rise and come upon them, but by necessity they hastened to him and fought with him. They mastered him, they detained him. They bound him with their body and their limbs, they overcame his death and his fire and his darkness.

[The] second time that they wept is [when the]ir father, the First Man, [ascend]ed from the [abyss] of darkness and left them behind; that is the time when he stripped [them off] and left them below. Indeed, when th[ey] s[aw] how the First Man had risen out of the abyss and [l]eft them behind, and that they were abandoned in the enmit[y, th]ey wept and were sore of heart. Still, what could they do, wishing [to go up after him? Yet by necessity they gave] their heart to every affliction. They [remained b]ehind and grew [s]ick under the pressure of the weighty burden of all the works, until the end time.

[The] third time that they wept is when the Living Spirit stripped off the three garments of activity, placing them beneath all things. He gave them a sign to lift their heads and rise to the heights from that place; and to pass and journey through all the earths until they should reach the land of tranquilli[t]y and peace, the place of rest prepared for them. So, when they had seen him, that he had separated himself from them, while they themselves remained behind after him and had not ascended; at that moment when they stayed behind these three garments wept. After their crying, they turned their [hear]t to all the heights that were concealed from them, and were of one mind. For [they would] soar up and come to the heights; and pass over all things until the time that was ordained for them all [should come] at the end of the worlds.

[The f]ourth time when they will weep is when the [S]tatue will be taken up on the last day, and they will weep [for] the souls of the liars and blasphemers; for they may give [them no help] because their limbs have been severed [and given to the powers] of the darkness. And also [th]ose souls, when the Statue will go up and they are left alo[n]e, they will weep in that they will rema[in] behind in affliction for ever. For they wi[ll be cut off] and separated from the Last Statue. An[d it is] a necessity to take these souls who are ready for loss as retribution for the deeds that they have done. They go i[n to] this [darkne]ss and are bound with the Darkness; just as they desired it and loved it, and placed their treasure with it. At that very moment, when the Last Statue rises up, the[y wi]ll weep. And then they will scream out loud because they will be severed from the company of this great Statue. And they remain behind for ever. This great weeping [and separation] is terrible, it occurs in front of the souls and [the spirits] who are ready for loss in accordance with their deeds. And they [will] weep with that crying, they will never be silent; because they will not attain rest from this time on.

So, they too are the garments of these elements. This fourth time of weeping is heart-rending for them. It is much worse for them than these other three times of weeping before. This fourth time the weeping is not for themselves. Rather they weep and are heartsore for these soul[s] who will be cut off from peace, because rest will not come about for them, to allow them to rest from torment for ever.

fills.explanation: The definite article correctly begins the sentence introducing the second time of weeping, matching the parallel structure of ¶3 ("the first time") and ¶5 ("the third time").
The spiritual reading identifies this as "the deepest state of falsity and evil," and the same paragraph later confirms "risen out of the abyss," making "abyss" the only consistent term.
The spiritual reading says "divested Himself of them"; "stripped them off" is the standard Kephalaia idiom for removing garments from oneself, consistent with the garment-imagery throughout.

fills.explanation: The garments wished to follow the First Man upward but could not; "by necessity" echoes ¶3's identical motif, and "gave their heart to every affliction" expresses the surrender of will described in the spiritual reading.
The definite article begins the sentence introducing the third time of weeping, following the identical syntactic pattern of the preceding two times.
The spiritual reading says "they were to ascend"; "they would" introduces the future-intentional sense of their aspiration to soar upward, matching the eschatological anticipation in this passage.

The spiritual reading says "to be fulfilled"; "should come" is the natural Kephalaia idiom for an appointed time arriving, completing the clause "until the time that was ordained for them all should come at the end of the worlds."

The spiritual reading says they "grieve over the souls"; "weep for" is the natural Kephalaia idiom expressing grief on behalf of others, and ¶7 explicitly confirms "they weep and are heartsore for these souls."

The spiritual reading says "no further means of restoration"; "give them no help" is the natural-plane rendering in the Kephalaia register, explaining why the garments weep — the severed limbs leave them powerless to aid these souls.

The spiritual reading says "given over to falsity from evil"; "given to the powers of the darkness" is standard Kephalaia phrasing for souls delivered to the archontic forces, and grammatically completes "severed and given to the powers of the darkness."

The spiritual reading says "of final separation"; "weeping and separation" pairs naturally with the passage's central theme of being severed from the Last Statue, and forms a hendiadys common in the Kephalaia register.
The spiritual reading explicitly identifies "the spirits" as the pair to "the souls"; in the Kephalaia, "souls and spirits" denotes the full interior being of those destined for loss.
The future tense is required by the eschatological context of the fourth weeping, consistent with "they will never be silent" immediately following and the future tense used throughout ¶6.
